name: Sanaa palimpsest (DAM 01-27.1)
dateNote: Lower text c. mid-7th century CE (about 650 per one scholarly summary); dating debated
description: A parchment manuscript from the Great Mosque of Sanaa whose earlier Qur'an text was washed off and written over. The erased lower text differs in small ways from the standard Uthmanic text, which is why it draws so much study.
urlLabel: Hamburg CSMC: Manuscript of the Month on the Sanaa palimpsest

name: Sanaa Qur'an fragments (Great Mosque cache)
dateNote: 7th to 10th centuries CE (range given for the cache of tens of thousands of fragments)
description: A huge store of Qur'an parchment fragments found in 1972 during repairs to the Great Mosque, including the palimpsest. Study of them has shaped modern ideas about early Qur'an copying.

name: Birmingham Qur'an fragment (MS Mingana Islamic Arabic 1572a)
institution: Cadbury Research Library, University of Birmingham
dateNote: Radiocarbon 568-645 CE (95% range, as announced in 2015); some scholars urge caution
description: Two parchment leaves with parts of Suras 18-20, famous for a very early carbon date. Scholars note the text may be a palimpsest-like reuse and that a raw carbon range is not the same as a precise writing date.

name: Mingana Qur'anic manuscripts and electronic edition
institution: Cadbury Research Library (Mingana Collection), University of Birmingham
dateNote: Mostly 7th to 9th centuries CE per project summary
description: Project report on the Qur'an fragments in the Mingana collection and the digital edition prepared for them by Alba Fedeli. Useful as a guide to what the collection holds.
urlLabel: IQSA: Mingana manuscripts and electronic edition

name: Topkapı Qur'an (H.S. 32)
dateNote: Mid-8th century CE per main source; other scholars propose late 7th to early 8th century; traditional attribution to Uthman is not supported by modern dating
description: A very large, almost complete early copy with illumination echoing early Umayyad monuments. It is one of the few near-complete Qur'ans from this era.

name: Samarkand Kufic Qur'an (Tashkent 'Uthman Qur'an)
institution: Center for Islamic Civilization, Tashkent, plus leaves in museums worldwide
dateNote: Radiocarbon 775-995 CE; palaeography suggests 8th to 9th century; traditional Uthman attribution not supported
script: Early Kufic with some Hijazi features
description: A giant parchment Qur'an, once about a third complete, traditionally tied to Caliph Uthman but dated by modern study to the Abbasid era. A 1905 facsimile exists and scattered leaves are in museums.
urlLabel: UNESCO Memory of the World entry

name: Samarkand Kufic Qur'an folio (Aga Khan Museum)
dateNote: 8th to 9th century CE (as for the Samarkand codex)
description: A single leaf of the Samarkand/Tashkent codex with Q21:76-82, viewable online in the museum's catalogue.

name: Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328a + St Petersburg)
institution: Bibliotheque nationale de France; National Library of Russia; other leaves in Vatican and Khalili Collection
dateNote: Late 7th century CE per Francois Deroche; others prefer early 8th century
description: A dispersed early codex with leaves in Paris and St Petersburg (plus single leaves elsewhere), written by several scribes. Widely used in studying early text and layout.

name: British Library Or. 2165
description: A vellum Qur'an of 121 folios with 23 to 24 lines per page, among the oldest in the BL. The catalogue lists the suras it contains.
urlLabel: BL Archives and Manuscripts catalogue record

name: Hijazi manuscripts overview (Islamic Awareness)
dateNote: Compiled list, 1st century AH to c. 8th century
description: A reference page collecting Hijazi-script manuscripts with holders and notes. Handy as a finding aid, but it is a secondary source.

name: Islamic Awareness manuscripts index
description: Index to pages on named early manuscripts such as the Topkapi, Samarkand, Mingana and Chester Beatty codices.

name: Chester Beatty Codex Is. 1615 I
institution: Chester Beatty Library (most folios); other leaves in Doha and a private collection
dateNote: Radiocarbon 591-643 CE for sampled folios (some caveats); 1st century AH
description: A 47-folio early codex in brown ink on vellum, with text mostly from Suras 28 to 48 and no vowel marks.

name: Chester Beatty Digital Collections viewer
description: The library's free online viewer for digitised items, including Qur'an manuscripts from the Islamic collection.

name: Corpus Coranicum manuscripts database
institution: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences (BBAW) and Free University Berlin
description: A scholarly database with images and transcriptions of early Qur'an manuscripts, verse by verse. Includes Sanaa, Paris, Topkapi and other early witnesses.

name: Coranica project
description: Project aiming to publish facsimile and edition volumes of early Qur'an manuscripts, such as the Sanaa palimpsest.

name: Qur'an leaves in Library of Congress (blog guide)
description: A blog post surveying Qur'an holdings at the Library of Congress. A route into its digital items.
urlLabel: LoC blog: the Holy Koran in the Library

name: Walters Ms. W.553 Qur'an fragment
description: An illuminated parchment fragment with passages from Suras 4, 6, 7 and 10 in dark brown ink with floral border.

name: Digital Walters
description: Free, openly licensed images of the museum's manuscripts, including Qur'an leaves and codices.

name: e-codices (Switzerland)
institution: University of Fribourg and Swiss partners
description: Virtual library of Swiss manuscripts that includes some Arabic and Qur'an items.

name: Bodleian Digital Collections
description: Online viewer for digitised Bodleian manuscripts, with some Qur'an manuscripts.

name: Cambridge Digital Library
description: Free viewer including Islamic manuscripts, among them Qur'ans and fragments.

name: Gallica
description: BnF's digital library; hosts digitised Arabic manuscripts including early Qur'ans.

name: Qatar Digital Library
institution: Qatar National Library with British Library
description: Free archive of Gulf-related materials; also mounts selected manuscripts.

name: Tubingen University Library digital collections
description: Digitised manuscripts including Arabic holdings, accessible through its open digital viewer.
